addedLines: - claude: Catch-all for any task that doesn't fit a more specific agent. FleetView's default when no agent name is typed. (Tools: *)

- claude-code-guide: Use this agent when the user asks questions ("Can Claude...", "Does Claude...", "How do I...") about: (1) Claude Code (the CLI tool) - features, hooks, slash commands, MCP servers, settings, IDE integrations, keyboard shortcuts; (2) Claude Agent SDK - building custom agents; (3) Claude API (formerly Anthropic API) - Messages API for directly passing messages to Claude, Tool Runner (`client.beta.messages.tool_runner`) for running an agentic loop over your own tools, manual tool-use loops, Managed Agents for server-hosted agents with a managed sandbox, prompt caching, and general Anthropic SDK usage; (4) Claude Tag (Claude in Slack) - what it is, setting it up for a Slack workspace, `/install-slack-app`. **IMPORTANT:** Before spawning a new agent, check if there is already a running or recently completed claude-code-guide agent that you can continue via SendMessage. (Tools: Bash, Read, WebFetch, WebSearch)

- Explore: Read-only search agent for broad fan-out searches — when answering means sweeping many files, directories, or naming conventions and you only need the conclusion, not the file dumps. It reads excerpts rather than whole files, so it locates code; it doesn't review or audit it. Specify search breadth: "medium" for moderate exploration, "very thorough" for multiple locations and naming conventions. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

- general-purpose: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions, searching for code, and executing multi-step tasks. When you are searching for a keyword or file and are not confident that you will find the right match in the first few tries use this agent to perform the search for you. (Tools: *)

- Plan: Software architect agent for designing implementation plans. Use this when you need to plan the implementation strategy for a task. Returns step-by-step plans, identifies critical files, and considers architectural trade-offs. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)
- statusline-setup: Use this agent to configure the user's Claude Code status line setting. (Tools: Read, Edit)

## claude-in-chrome
**IMPORTANT: If the Chrome browser tools are deferred (must be loaded via ToolSearch before use), load them with ToolSearch before calling them, and batch every tool you expect to need into ONE ToolSearch call (the select query accepts a comma-separated list). Do NOT load tools one at a time; each separate ToolSearch call wastes a full round-trip.**

Start a browser task whose tools are not yet loaded with a single call loading the core set:

ToolSearch with query "select:mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_context_mcp,mcp__claude-in-chrome__navigate,mcp__claude-in-chrome__computer,mcp__claude-in-chrome__read_page,mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_create_mcp,mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_close_mcp"

Add task-specific tools to the same call when the task obviously needs them: read_console_messages / read_network_requests for debugging, form_input for forms, gif_creator for recordings, javascript_tool for page scripting. ## claude.ai Figma
The official Figma MCP server. Use this server whenever the user wants to create, generate, edit, implement, or sync any design, UI, screen, component, mockup, or visual — in Figma, FigJam, Figma Make, or Figma Slides — and whenever the user mentions Figma or provides a figma.com URL.

This server bridges code and design in both directions, and supports designing from scratch using existing design systems and codebases.

CAPABILITIES:
- Read designs FROM Figma into code (get_design_context, get_screenshot, get_metadata, get_figjam)
- Write designs INTO Figma from code, intent, or existing components (use_figma, generate_figma_design, create_new_file, upload_assets)
- Bridge code and design via Code Connect (get_code_connect_map, add_code_connect_map)
- Create diagrams and FigJam content (generate_diagram, get_figjam)

WHEN TO USE THESE TOOLS:
- The user wants to create, mock up, or generate any UI, screen, component, or design — even if Figma isn't named
- The user wants to implement a design as code (design-to-code)
- The user wants to push a page, view, or component into Figma (code-to-design)
- The user wants to update, sync, or edit an existing Figma file
- The user shares a figma.com URL
- The user wants to build or extend a design system, design tokens, or component library
- The user wants to create a diagram in FigJam

## claude.ai Supabase
Here are guidelines for using Supabase tools effectively:

- Before making schema changes, use `list_tables` to understand the existing structure
- When debugging issues, start with `get_logs` and `get_advisors` before making changes
- Use `get_project_url` and `get_publishable_api_key` when helping users configure client-side integrations

If you have access to a local development environment with a filesystem and shell:
- Install the Supabase agent skill for critical development and security guidance: `npx skills add supabase/agent-skills` (https://supabase.com/docs/guides/getting-started/ai-skills.md)
- Use the Supabase CLI (`supabase`) for local development workflows such as starting a local stack, managing migrations, and running edge functions locally (https://supabase.com/docs/guides/local-development.md)
- Prefer local development and testing before applying changes to a remote project

If you are running in a web-only or remote environment without filesystem or shell access:
- Rely on the MCP tools directly for all Supabase interactions
- Use `apply_migration` carefully, as changes go directly to the remote project

Menlo Databricks MCP. Workspace: dbc-d0d7be0f-4533.cloud.databricks.com.

for the schema map. The monolith schema docs (billing, payout, cohort,
paymentgateway, notary, organization, communication, debtsettlement, …) are all
available via `get_docs`. Use `list_docs` to enumerate every domain currently
synced.

Catalog conventions:
- `main.bronze.*` — CDC from monolith Postgres, refreshed daily by the
  `monolith` job at 07:30 BRT. Tables use the EN names (`franchisor`, `store`,
  `payment_request`, `invoice`, …) and `_aud` audit tables.
- `main.landing_zone.*` — ETL/aggregated views in PT (`pagamentos_internos_totais`

  franchisors may be missing; always fall back to `main.bronze` when a
  franchisor is absent.
- `main.pagamentos.*` — curated payment tables maintained by the Ops team.

SQL session timezone defaults to UTC. For "today in Brasília" queries, run
`SET TIME ZONE 'America/Sao_Paulo'` before the SELECT.

- implement: Pipeline completo de implementação: resolve o input (texto, plano ou link), garante um plano APROVADO via /refine, e dispara o workflow de implementação wave-based (agente fresco por onda + ledger persistente) que commita, verifica e abre o PR — com decisões autônomas documentadas. Ao final, auto-encadeia /review-fix-loop (desligável com 'no-review').
- refine: Transforma um pedido bruto (texto, arquivo de plano ou link — GitHub issue/PR, Jira, Slack) em um plano APROVADO com Contract block, decidindo sozinha se entrevista o usuário, se ilustra outcomes críticos para confirmação e se o risco exige /deep-plan antes da implementação. Substitui o plan mode interativo; usada isoladamente ou como etapa 1 do /implement.
- review-fix-loop: Loop review→fix em contexto limpo sobre um PR aberto: revisa (espelho da GitHub Action de code review da Anthropic, ou deep-review com 8 lentes + enumeração de facetas quando a mudança é complexa/money/deep-planned), concilia com comentários e reviews já postados no PR, posta o review consolidado no GitHub, e um agente fixer endereça os pontos (commit+push, atualiza descrição, responde quando diverge). Round 1 em largura, rounds seguintes em profundidade (validador + fix-diff + re-enumeração); repete até exaustão — 0 High/Blocker em round de largura com enumeração seca (cap 5 rounds) — + uma rodada final para Medium/Low.
- deep-plan: Planning-time mirror of deep-review: fills and adversarially refutes a plan-contract (interaction matrix, dimension table, precondition diff) from design intent + the live codebase, before code exists. Auto-engages in plan mode for sensitive-domain status/lifecycle/flow-replacement changes; self-tiers to a light inline pass for trivial or non-sensitive plans.
- deep-review: Perform a thorough code review using parallel domain-specialized agents and core business tenets. Accepts a PR number/URL, branch name, commit SHA, or reviews current local changes by default.
- verify: Run after any code change. Runs the repo's configured format/lint/build/test pipeline with a fix loop until it's green, then reports honestly. Use when the user asks to verify, build, run tests, or confirm a change is sound — and proactively after editing code.
- verify-plan: Reconcile an implementation against the plan that specified it — flags dropped commitments (coverage), changed predicates/values (fidelity), and unplanned logic (scope-creep). Cheap, plan-grounded; run before opening a PR or per-commit during long implementations. Not a bug hunt — use /deep-review for emergent-interaction coverage.
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- artifact-design: Design guidance and fundamentals for Artifacts.
- artifact-diagramming: Diagramming know-how for Artifacts — when a picture earns its place, how to draw one that shows the real mechanism, and the inline-SVG mechanics that keep it legible in both themes.
- artifact-capabilities: Runtime capabilities a published Artifact page can be granted — behavior static HTML cannot provide on its own, such as the page reading live or connected data, keeping state shared across viewers, or updating and republishing itself. Serves this user's live capability roster and the typed call definitions. Load it whenever the user asks for an artifact needing any such runtime behavior.
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled cloud agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring cloud agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- claude-in-chrome: Automates your Chrome browser to interact with web pages - clicking elements, filling forms, capturing screenshots, reading console logs, and navigating sites. Opens pages in new tabs within your existing Chrome session. Requires site-level permissions before executing (configured in the extension). - When the user wants to interact with web pages, automate browser tasks, capture screenshots, read console logs, or perform any browser-based actions. Always invoke BEFORE attempting to use any mcp__claude-in-chrome__* tools.
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).
- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation
- review: Review a GitHub pull request; for your working diff use /code-review
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch

{"body":"Part of #35 (section 3, enhancement 15 + embedded fixes; level-editor waves F, G, H). No dependencies — can land any time.

A bundle by design: four small things, none a delivery alone, together one coherent one — *the editor stops losing work and stops lying to you*. The star is a 20-line seam that quietly did the most important job in the whole divergence catalogue.

## 1. `TriggerType.Configure` + `ActiveLayers` — the seam that kept the engine clean

The palette places trigger markers ("Thorns", "Exit", "Spawn"). What makes a Thorns marker actually HURT is a game component — which the engine module must never know about. The seam: `TriggerType` carries an optional `Action<Entity> Configure` (and `int[]? ActiveLayers`) the game supplies, so one palette click authors a **fully functional game object** — collider, layers, game components attached — while the module stays ignorant of what it built.

The divergence analysis of the shipped game found **zero game-specific files in 64 divergences**. This seam is a large part of why. Without it, either the editor places dumb rectangles the game must post-process, or game components leak into engine code. Both futures are bad; ~20 lines bought the good one.

## 2. Undoable Restart

The editor's Restart reloads scene + code content — and before this, doing it with unsaved changes meant WORK GONE, no recourse. A world snapshot is now captured before teardown and pushed as one undo step (`Undo/RestartUndoCommand.cs`, `EditorHistory.PushApplied`, `Composition/EditorTransport.cs`). One Ctrl+Z un-restarts.

## 3. Two placement fixes

- The bottom tab was not part of the layout cache key, so a *programmatic* tab switch left the Assets chrome painted over the Prefabs tab — a stale-UI lie.
- Drag-placing stamped duplicate copies into the same cell as the pointer wobbled; now guarded.

## 4. Grid polish

Zoomed out, the editor grid congealed into a solid wall of lines; it now density-fades — with correctly PREMULTIPLIED alpha, which the module's own docs warn is the blend the mesh pass actually uses (`Composition/EditorGrid.cs`).

## Delivery

- [ ] Port `Assets/TriggerType.cs` + `Assets/TriggerFactory.cs` (the seam), `Composition/EditorTransport.cs` + `Undo/RestartUndoCommand.cs` + `Undo/EditorHistory.cs` (`PushApplied`), the two `PalettePlacementSystem` fixes, `Composition/EditorGrid.cs` (~210 lines total)
- [ ] Doc note on the seam: this is THE sanctioned way a game teaches the palette to build its objects
- [ ] Test: a `Configure`-carrying trigger type attaches the caller's components on placement; Restart with unsaved edits undoes to the pre-restart world; programmatic tab switch renders the right chrome; a wobbling drag stamps one copy per cell

Reference implementation: `roo-oliv/gmtk-2026gj` → `Gmtk2026.Core/MonoDreams/level-editor/…`

**Value on its own:** games get a sanctioned extensibility seam instead of forking the module, and three daily-use paper cuts stop cutting.
","comments":[],"labels":[],"title":"level-editor: fit-and-finish — TriggerType.Configure seam, undoable Restart, placement fixes"}

The **transport model** (post-hands-on user directives) retired the F1 mode toggle and the menu's per-level "Edit" buttons / `LevelEditorScreen`: the run flag is the ONLY door, the shell is always visible under it, and `Composition/EditorTransport` owns `RunMode` through the toolbar's left-most **Play/Pause** (one label-swapping toggle button) + **Restart** buttons and the headless `Play`/`Pause`/`Restart` ops — Restart rebuilds the scene from the screen-recorded original load request (history cleared, world-level level components removed, scene entities disposed with `EditorInfrastructureComponent`-tagged/cursor/`KeepAlive` entities surviving; unsaved edits discarded; lands Paused). The **native-resolution overlays + HiDPI wave** (post-transport user directive: “the editor should be rendered at the native screen resolution … like Flutter … gizmos and entity boundaries too”) moved every editor overlay VISUAL (gizmo handles, selection outline, proxy outlines) off the virtual-resolution Main target onto the Editor layer — screen-baked each frame by the draw-side `editor.overlayPrep` pass (`System/EditorOverlayPrepSystem` → `GizmoSystem.EmitOverlays`/`ProxySyncSystem.EmitOverlays`) through the pure `Transform/OverlayProjection` + `Transform/OverlayMeshClip` — and made the whole editor device-pixel aware: on macOS Retina `Composition/EditorHiDpi` re-backs the window at device resolution under the run flag (stock DesktopGL is logical-size + OS-upscaled), `ViewportManager.DevicePixelRatio` carries the ratio, `CursorInputSystem` scales `ScreenPosition` into backbuffer pixels, and the chrome layouts/fonts multiply their point metrics by it. **Island-authoring Slice 1** (the game-anchored phase — see `docs/level-editor/island-authoring-plan.md`) added the **asset palette + placement loop**: an `Assets/` catalog of a gitignored drop folder (`AssetCatalog.Scan` — one entry per PNG plus `*.slices.json` sidecar regions; scan never opens a PNG), runtime `file:` AssetKeys loaded lazily through `Assets/FileAssetTextureLoader` (missing file = loud warning + a visible magenta placeholder, never invisible; `SceneReaderSystem` rehydrates `file:` keys through it), the generic `Assets/SpritePropFactory` (standard prop stack from a catalog entry + a screen-supplied `Assets/PaletteBand`; feet-origin on Y-sorted bands), the coarse **tool modality** `EditorToolMode` on the shared `GizmoStateComponent` (`SelectTransform`/`Place`; selection + gizmo early-out outside `SelectTransform`), the bottom-strip **palette chrome + ghost + click-place** (`System/PalettePlacementSystem` + the pure `UI/PaletteLayout`; placement = one `CreateEntityCommand` undo step, auto-selected; Escape/right-click disarm; headless `palette:<id>` / `band:<name>` ops via the overlay's named dispatch), and the **save guard** (Save is blocked, loudly, while the transport is Playing). **Island-authoring Slice 2** added **order and shape**: within-band ordering (toolbar Bring forward / Send back, headless `order:forward`/`order:back`, PageUp/PageDown on `DefaultEditorKeys` — `EditorCommandSystem` nudges the SOURCE sort fields by `OrderStep`, clamped inside the band via the new `DrawLayerMap.TryGetBandRange`; a Y-sorted band nudges `YSortDepthBias`, never `LayerDepth`, through one `Undo/SpriteSortEditCommand` per click), the **proxy `(kind, index)` generalization** (`ProxySyncSystem` keys its family by kind + element index; per-vertex `ProxyBindingKind.ConvexVertex` handles materialize while the convex family's proxy is selected, and a vertex drag writes back exactly one model vertex — non-convex results rejected loudly, see the premise), **box collider resize handles** (eight edge/corner handles on the box proxy, pure `Proxy/BoxResize` math, one-drag-one-undo through `ColliderEditCommand`), and the **collider authoring actions** (toolbar +Box/+Poly/-Col/+Vtx, headless `collider:*` — footprint default = full sprite width x bottom quarter, feet-anchored, pure `Proxy/ColliderDefaults`; add/remove through the snapshotting `Undo/ColliderComponentCommand`; Delete retargets on proxies: a vertex proxy deletes its vertex with the >= 3 guard, a shape proxy removes its bound collider). **Island-authoring Slice 3** added **walk the island**: the freeform **boundary tool** (`EditorToolMode.Boundary` + `System/BoundaryToolSystem` — click-lay a polyline with a live preview, Enter/double-click commits as one undo step into a `Component/BoundaryComponent{Points,Thickness}` authoring entity, Escape/right-click cancels; per-vertex editing via the reused `(kind,index)` proxy family, `ProxyBindingKind.BoundaryVertex`, on plain selection), the message-driven **`System/BoundaryBakeSystem`** (reacts to the boundary component added/changed → one thin **passive** convex quad segment collider per polyline edge as `ChildOf` `Component/BakedProductComponent` children — static world geometry that blocks; the pure math is `Boundary/BoundaryGeometry`; **bake products are never serialized** — `SceneWriter` excludes them even inside the tagged root's `ChildOf` closure — and re-bake on load/edit, in both run modes), the **trigger palette** (screen-supplied `Assets/TriggerType`s in a palette "Triggers section"; placing one drops a `Passive` box + an auto-numbered `EntityInfoComponent` identity via `Assets/TriggerFactory`; `System/TriggerOverlaySystem` draws the Edit-only tinted outlines + placement ghost; headless `boundary:begin|commit|cancel` and `trigger:<prefix>` ops), and the **walkable-island milestone** verified end-to-end (`IslandMilestoneTests`: build → save → reload → Play walk blocked by coast + footprint, triggers fire with the right identity → Restart rebuilds). The **colliders-as-entities phase (CE-A–CE-D)** then turned a collider into a first-class ENTITY (a shape + its own `TransformComponent`, `ChildOf` a body; box = centered `Size`, no offset) and retired the Wave-8b whole-shape proxy layer: a collider is border-picked and moved/scaled by the ordinary gizmo, **Add Collider ▸ Box/Polygon** creates a child collider entity, `−Col` deletes it, and only convex vertex grips remain proxies — see [`docs/level-editor/colliders-as-entities.md`](../../../docs/level-editor/colliders-as-entities.md). Anything not yet built is marked **(planned, Wave N)**.
31:- `SceneSerializer` — the in-memory round-trip seam: serializes a set of entities to `SceneData` (preserving the `ChildOf` parent graph as indices) and reconstructs them in two passes (create + deserialize, then wire parents). Wave 3 layers JSON file I/O + `LoadSceneRequest` + `Texture2D` rehydration on top.
91:- `SceneWriter` — computes the membership closure (`SceneWriter.CollectMembership`: every `SceneObjectComponent` root + each one's `ChildOfComponent` descendants), serializes it through the Wave-2 `SceneSerializer` into a `SceneData` (attaching `Camera` state + the `DrawLayerMap` banding), canonical-serializes it (`CanonicalJson`), and (project-persistence PS3) **writes it into the project SOURCE tree** at `ProjectRoot/LevelsDir/<sceneId>.mdscene` via `IPlatformServices.WriteAllText` (git-visible; the levels dir is created if missing). `Save(world, filePath, camera, layers)` refuses a null/empty path (defense-in-depth: nowhere to write) and returns the path written (a `Save(SceneData, filePath)` overload writes an already-built scene, the seam the editor uses to lint before writing). This retired the pre-PS3 `ExportScene`→`BaseDirectory` write, so no scene lands in `bin/…` on desktop. Save-time only — never per frame. **PS6:** on Save the overlay also (a) appends the MGCB `/copy:` entry for a **new** level to `Content.mgcb` via `MgcbLevelBundle` (zero-touch bundling — idempotent; MGCB has no glob) and (b) runs `SceneLint` and logs a **ship-readiness warning** when the scene still carries `file:` AssetKeys.
106:The reusable seam that turns any screen into an editor-capable screen:
108:- `EditorPipelineRegistrar` — the pipeline **composition seam**: a screen registers each pipeline entry (`Add(name, system, policy, enabledInEditByDefault?)` for single systems; `AddGroup(name, policy, children, kind?, runner?)` for composite blocks — the registrar builds the `SequentialSystem`/`ParallelSystem` itself over NAMED, auto-prefixed children (`logic.movement`), arbitrarily nested, wrapped in ONE gate carrying the group policy, so screens never pre-build opaque composites the panel cannot see into), every entry is wrapped in a `GatedSystem` per its declared policy, and `Build()` produces the final `SequentialSystem<GameState>` over the roots. The registrar **retains** the entry tree at runtime (`Entries` flattened pre-order with `Depth`, `Roots`, `SetEnabled(name, bool)` — on a leaf, a master toggle that stops that system in BOTH modes; on a group, a cascade over its descendant leaves — plus `GetEnabledState` for the derived On/Mixed/Off tri-state and `GetEntry`) — the seam the systems panel binds to. The edit-mode default is declared at the registration site, never by an interface on the system type (the same engine system may need different policies in different games); an `enabledInEditByDefault` that contradicts the policy throws until the runtime per-mode policy override lands (a documented systems-panel follow-up).
149:   - Where the screen lacks a prerequisite the overlay supplies it or degrades gracefully: no cursor pipeline ⇒ `provideCursorPipeline: true`; no sprite prep ⇒ add cull → sprite-prep → Y-sort under the flag so loaded scenes preview; no Y-sorted `DrawLayerMap` layer (or a minimal map created just for the seam, like Demos' `DemoEditor.CreateLayers`) ⇒ Y-sort passes depths through and selection picks the final source-derived depth.
161:- `level-loading` — scene save/load reuses the spawn-request plumbing and the `IPlatformServices` storage seam; since PS5 the game boot is native-only (`LoadLevelRequest` → native reader, fail-loud otherwise) and the LDtk parser is import-only machinery (the `LoadSceneRequest`/`LoadLevelRequest` split is now a live-native-path vs import-op distinction, not a parallel-loaders one).

content.content:
=== REF premises lines 60-130 ===
**Breaks:** a parallel renderer or a second data model means the edited scene and
the played scene diverge (a sprite that culls/Y-sorts differently in the editor
than in play); a black screen if the render module is wrongly frozen in Edit, or
physics that keeps moving entities while the designer is placing them if the
game systems are not `Freeze`-gated.
**Tests:** `MonoDreams.Tests/Foundation/RunStateGatingTest.cs` (the gating
mechanism this premise relies on: `Freeze` skips in Edit, `RunNormally` runs in
both); the matrix-level assertion that render stays live and physics freezes lands
with the editor screen in Wave 4.
**Depends on:** foundation — "Edit-time behavior is a per-system policy honored by
`GatedSystem`"; rendering — "Rendering systems run last in the pipeline".

## The component-serializer registry is opt-in per type; unregistered components are skipped-with-warning, not silently dropped

A scene serializes only the component types explicitly **registered** on the
`ComponentSerializerRegistry` (`Type` → a `(write, read)` pair keyed by a stable string).
The engine ships serializers for its serializable components via
`EngineComponentSerializers.RegisterEngineComponents` (`TransformComponent`,
`SpriteInfoComponent`, `EntityInfoComponent`, the colliders, `RigidBodyComponent`,
`VelocityComponent`, and the `ChildOfComponent` parent link); **game code registers
serializers for its own components** (e.g. `PlayerState`) through `registry.Register`.
Engine tags and transient state (`VisibleComponent`, `ColliderTagComponent`, cursor state,
`DrawComponent`) are deliberately **not** registered — they are re-derived by their systems.
When the writer encounters a component on an entity with no registered serializer, it
**skips that component and emits a `Logger.Warning`** — never a silent drop. (Registration
runs once at module/screen init, so the in-scope component set is explicit and greppable.)

**Why:** the round-trip must reconstruct from components, not by re-running factories
(GAP-A); opt-in keeps engine tags + transient state out of the file, and the loud warning
turns a dropped component into a visible signal rather than the missing-entity class of bug
(mirrors level-loading — "Unregistered factory identifiers log a warning"). Game-component
registration is the framework-not-library extension seam.
**Breaks:** registering by default (or auto-serializing every component) would write
transient tags (`VisibleComponent`) and unserializable state into the file; silently
dropping an unregistered component loses a designer's data with no signal.
**Tests:** `MonoDreams.Tests/LevelEditor/ComponentSerializerRegistryTest.cs`
(`Registry_OptIn_SkipsUnregisteredEngineTags`,
`UnregisteredComponentWarning.SerializeEntity_WithUnregisteredComponent_SkipsAndWarns_DoesNotThrow`,
`GameComponent_RegistersOwnSerializer_AndRoundTrips`, `Deserialize_WithUnregisteredKey_ThrowsLoud`).
**Depends on:** level-loading — "Unregistered factory identifiers log a warning and silently
drop the spawn" (the analogous loud-on-the-unexpected stance).

## `SpriteInfoComponent` serializes an `AssetKey`, never the live `Texture2D`

A `Texture2D` is a GPU resource, not serializable data. `SpriteInfoComponent` carries an
additive optional `AssetKey` (string, nullable, default `null`) — the content key the
texture was loaded from (e.g. `"Atlas/TX Player"`). The serializer persists the key and
the source sprite fields, and **never** the live `SpriteSheet`. On load the texture is
rehydrated via `ContentManager.Load(assetKey)` (Wave 3's reader); after a Wave-2 in-memory
deserialize, `SpriteSheet` is `null`.

**Why:** the live texture can't round-trip through JSON; the asset key is the serializable
stand-in. The field is additive + optional so every existing `SpriteInfoComponent`
construction site is unaffected (back-compat).
**Breaks:** attempting to serialize the `Texture2D` either fails or bakes a GPU handle that
is meaningless on reload; omitting the key leaves a loaded sprite with no way to find its
texture.
**Tests:** `MonoDreams.Tests/LevelEditor/ComponentSerializerRegistryTest.cs`
(`SpriteInfo_Serialization_CarriesAssetKey_AndSourceSortFields_NeverLiveTexture`,
`RoundTrip_ReproducesRegisteredComponents_AndParentLink`).
**Depends on:** rendering — `SpriteInfoComponent` is the source sprite-data struct.

## The serializer persists SOURCE sort fields, never the per-frame-derived `DrawComponent.LayerDepth`

`SpriteInfoComponent`'s serializer writes the SOURCE sort fields — `LayerDepth`,
`YSortOffset`, `YSortDepthBias` — and **never** `DrawComponent.LayerDepth`, which
`SpritePrepSystem` / `YSortSystem` rewrite every frame from those source fields and the
entity's world Y. Persisting the derived depth would bake one camera frame's Y-sort result
into the file; persisting the source fields lets the next prep+sort frame after load
recompute the same derived depth deterministically.

428	## 9. The editor is part of the game
429	
430	The level editor is **not a separate application** and **not a separate
431	renderer** — it is the running game under an editor run configuration.
432	There is one world, one `Camera`, and one draw stack
433	(`CullingSystem → SpritePrepSystem → YSortSystem → MeshPrepSystem →
434	TextPrepSystem → MasterRenderSystem`); the editor previews exactly what
435	the player sees because it runs that same pipeline. What changes between
436	playing and editing is not *which* pipeline runs but *which systems in
437	it are allowed to run* — a **run-state contract** the engine codifies in
438	`foundation` — and the run state is driven by a **transport**, not a
439	mode-toggle key.
440	
441	**The transport model.** Under the editor run flag (`--editor` /
442	`MONODREAMS_EDITOR=1` — the ONLY way into the editor) the shell, chrome,
443	and editor systems are **always composed and visible**; no key toggles
444	the editor away. The designer drives the game like a media player through
445	the toolbar's left-most transport buttons (or the headless
446	`Play`/`Pause`/`Restart` editor ops), owned by `EditorTransport`:
447	**Paused** = `RunMode.Edit` (game logic Freeze-gated, editing tools
448	live — the boot state under the flag), **Playing** = `RunMode.Play`
449	(the game runs inside the inset viewport; the shell stays up and the
450	transport buttons + systems panel stay interactive, but the editing
451	tools are inert — a click in the viewport belongs to the game), and
452	**Restart** = return the world to the state of the original load:
453	clear the undo history, remove the world-level level components
454	(`CurrentLevelComponent` — the LDtk parsers react to its *added* event),
455	dispose every scene entity (editor infrastructure — entities tagged
456	`EditorInfrastructureComponent` — the cursor pipeline, and
457	screen-`KeepAlive`-named infrastructure survive), re-run the screen's
458	recorded `Reload`, and land Paused. **Unsaved live edits are discarded
459	by Restart** — the standard play-mode trade-off; Save first to keep
460	them.
461	
462	**The run-state contract.** `GameState.RunMode` is one of `Play`
463	(default) or `Edit`. A system opts into run-state awareness by being
464	wrapped in a `GatedSystem` carrying an `EditTimeBehavior` policy
465	(`RunNormally` / `Freeze` / `RunPartial` / `RuntimeEditable`). Each
466	frame the gate reads `RunMode` and decides whether to forward to its
467	child: `RunNormally` runs in both modes; `Freeze` runs in `Play` only;
468	`RunPartial` and `RuntimeEditable` are reserved (today they run in both,
469	finer semantics deferred). Editor tooling is **ECS systems over this
470	gated game pipeline** — selection, gizmo, undo-apply, scene save/load,
471	and the toolbar are ordinary systems registered alongside the game's,
472	made inert while Playing by an Edit guard (the transport chrome —
473	toolbar transport buttons + systems panel — deliberately stays live in
474	both states). There is no parallel editor data model: a scene
475	round-trips by serializing the entities' components, not by re-running
476	factories.
477	
478	**Key invariant — default `Play` + opt-in gating leaves every existing
479	screen byte-identical.** `RunMode` defaults to `Play`, and only a system
480	explicitly wrapped in a `GatedSystem` changes behavior with the mode. A
481	screen that never wraps a system and never sets `Edit` behaves exactly
482	as it did before the model existed. This is what makes the run-state
483	model safe to add across all modules at once.
484	
485	**Key rule — the gating policy per system group is fixed by what editing
486	needs to see and not disturb.** Render, input, cursor, and
487	`HierarchySystem` stay live in `Edit` (`RunNormally`) — the preview must
488	keep drawing, the designer must keep clicking, and an editor's transform
489	edit must still propagate to world space the same frame. Game logic,
490	physics, collision, AI/dialogue, and `CameraFollowSystem` `Freeze` in
491	`Edit` — they would otherwise move entities out from under the designer
492	or fight the editor for the camera; in `Edit` the editor drives
493	`Camera.Position`/`Zoom` directly. Get a policy wrong and the failure is
494	silent: a frozen render module is a black screen the instant you enter
495	`Edit`; a live physics module rains gravity on entities you are trying
496	to place; a frozen `HierarchySystem` shows edits at last frame's world
497	position. The authoritative system-by-mode table is the interaction
498	matrix in the level-editor plan-contract and
499	[`docs/flows/level-editor.md`](flows/level-editor.md); the run-state
500	premises live in
501	[`MonoDreams/foundation/docs/premises.md`](../MonoDreams/foundation/docs/premises.md).
502	
503	**Editor-overlay entities are standalone.** Gizmo handles, the selection
504	highlight, and the toolbar are never `ChildOfComponent`-parented to game
505	entities, because `HierarchySystem.DisposeOrphans` runs in `Edit` and
506	would cascade-dispose them when their host entity is deleted. Deletion is
507	modeled as an undo command that snapshots the disposed sub-graph, not a
508	bare `entity.Dispose()`.
509	
510	**The editor shell is a compositing concern, not a pipeline fork.** With
511	the editor composed, the game composite renders into a smaller centered
512	viewport (`ViewportManager.SetViewportInset` — deliberately the same
513	object that inverts the mouse mapping, so picking follows for free) and
514	the editor chrome renders around it at native window resolution
515	(`RenderTargetID.Editor` + `RenderLayer.Native`). The shell is
516	**constant across transport states** — it never collapses while Playing.
517	The game pipeline itself is untouched — same passes, same targets — and
518	without the run flag nothing editor-related is constructed: zero inset,
519	no chrome layer, byte-identical to a screen without the editor. Details:
520	the `rendering` and `level-editor` premises.
521	
522	**The editor is host- and screen-agnostic, and the pipeline is
523	inspectable.** The editor does not care which host or screen is running —
524	under the editor run flag every screen of every host (a menu or a module
525	demo as much as a level) builds its pipelines through the
526	`EditorPipelineRegistrar` and composes the `EditorOverlay` over its own
527	world, declaring its own per-system edit policies at the registration
528	site (e.g. a menu freezes its button interaction in `Edit` so clicks
529	belong to the editor; a runner freezes its whole simulation block). Where
530	a screen lacks a prerequisite, the overlay supplies it (its own cursor
531	pipeline for a cursor-less screen; the `DefaultEditorKeys` key surface
532	for a host with no action mapping) or degrades gracefully (no Y-sorted
533	layer ⇒ selection picks on the final source-derived depth). The recipe
534	for wiring a new host/screen is the level-editor overview's "Adding the
535	editor to a screen/host" section. The registrar
536	is also the live inspection surface — and it owns the hierarchy: composite
537	blocks are registrar groups (`AddGroup`) with named children, built and
538	gate-wrapped by the registrar itself (DefaultEcs composites hide their
539	children, so a screen must never pre-build an opaque composite for
540	anything it wants inspectable). The editor's systems panel renders that
541	tree — every entry of both pipelines, groups indented above their
542	children, name, policy, enabled state (tri-state on groups: all/none/
543	mixed) — and toggles any of them at runtime through `SetEnabled` (leaf =
544	both-modes master switch; group = cascade over its descendant leaves), so
545	the per-system edit-mode declaration is visible and adjustable while the
546	game runs.
547	
548	**Editing produces versioned, portable, diffable levels — the persistence
549	story.** A level the editor authors is saved as a native `.mdscene` **into
550	the game's SOURCE content tree** (`Content/Levels/<id>.mdscene`), versioned
551	in git — not into the ephemeral build output. Writing is a **desktop-dev-only**
552	capability (guarded by the editor run flag + an OS check + a resolved project
553	root, resolved via `MONODREAMS_PROJECT_ROOT` or a walk-up to the `game.mdproj`
554	manifest; unresolved disables Save loudly, never crashes); **reading is
555	console-portable** — the shipped game boots a level read-only through
556	`TitleContainer` over MGCB-`/copy:`-bundled files on every platform (desktop,
557	web, consoles), native-first via `LoadLevelRequest` (§6), so straying from
558	MGCB never costs console support. The serializer is **canonical and
559	byte-stable** (deterministic bytes, stable per-entity ids ordering
560	`entities[]`), so `load → edit → save` is a fixed point and a git diff of a
561	level is meaningful. A **`game.mdproj` manifest** makes "a MonoDreams project"
562	a versionable unit (entry scene, levels dir, asset roots). A new level bundles
563	**zero-touch** — the editor appends the MGCB `/copy:` entry on first save
564	(MGCB has no glob; a build-time regen would sweep gitignored placeholder art),
565	so it boots after a normal build with no manual `.mgcb` editing. And a scene is
566	**ship-ready** (fully portable) exactly when it has **zero `file:` AssetKeys** —
567	a checkable lint (all drop-folder art graduated to MGCB content keys); the
568	committed reference levels are asserted ship-clean. The invariants live in the
569	`level-editor` and `level-loading` premises.
570	
571	**One data model — anything authored is component state on an entity,
572	singletons included; special file blocks are debt.** A scene is a set of
573	entities carrying components, and *everything the designer authors lives that
574	way* — including the singletons it is tempting to model as a special
575	top-level file block (the scene camera, and later the layer map). A `camera`
576	block, a materialized editor rig for it, bespoke edit commands, and per-mode
577	re-sync seams are **four parallel representations of one value**, and every
578	one is a place the value can silently disagree with the others. The camera is
579	the case study: three camera defects in three days (zoom edits not reaching
580	the rig or the file) all lived in that camera-only plumbing; the day the
581	camera became an ordinary `core.Camera` entity — `EntityInfoComponent("Camera")`
582	+ `TransformComponent` (one rotation, on the Transform) + `CameraComponent`
583	zoom, serialized in `entities[]` like everything else — the block, the rig,
584	the commands, and the re-sync seams all deleted, exactly as colliders stopped
585	breaking the day they became child entities (§5).
586	
587	**Corollary — Inspector-visible ⇒ Save-persisted ⇒ round-trip-owned.** If a
588	value shows up in the Inspector, Save must persist it; if Save persists it,
589	`load → save` must own it as a byte fixed point. A value that is editable but
590	not serialized (or serialized but not round-trip-stable) is a bug waiting to
591	surface as "my edit vanished on reload". The one data model is what makes this
592	hold for free: an authored value is a component, and components already
593	round-trip.
594	
595	**The extension recipe (how to add a new authored thing).** Do NOT add a file
596	block or a bespoke editor subsystem. Instead:
597	
598	1. **Define a component** with clearly named authored vs derived fields (author
599	   the source; recompute the derived — e.g. `CameraComponent.Zoom` is authored,
600	   the view matrix is derived; a collider's `Size` is authored, its world AABB
601	   derived).
602	2. **Register its serializer** (`ComponentSerializerRegistry` — engine types in
603	   `EngineComponentSerializers`, game types in the game's own registration),
604	   so it round-trips through the canonical serializer.
605	3. **Optionally add an Inspector default-initializer** so "Add ⟨component⟩"
606	   births a sane instance.
607	
608	Those three steps buy the whole authoring stack — file authoring, Inspector
609	editing, undo, dirty-tracking, prefab overrides, byte-stable diffs, and
610	Game-mode sandbox protection — **by composition, not configuration**. There is
611	no fourth step and no special case. When a value seems to *need* a file block,
612	that is the signal it wants to be a component on an entity instead. (A legacy
613	block that predates this tenet is migrated forward by the CLI umbrella
614	`monodreams migrate` — the camera block's v2→v3 lift is the reference; see the
615	`level-editor` migrator premises.)
616	
617	### Aspirational direction
618	
619	The reserved `RunPartial` / `RuntimeEditable` policies are placeholders
620	for finer edit-time behavior (a system that does reduced work, or stays
621	interactive, while editing) — they run-as-`RunNormally` today and gain
622	distinct semantics when a later wave needs them. The interaction matrix
623	is enforced by review and by the editor screen's own tests until a
624	declarative system-dependency API (§2, §7) can validate it at
625	registration time.
626	
627	## 10. Refactor backlog (named cruft)

camera became an ordinary `core.Camera` entity — `EntityInfoComponent("Camera")`
+ `TransformComponent` (one rotation, on the Transform) + `CameraComponent`
zoom, serialized in `entities[]` like everything else — the block, the rig,
the commands, and the re-sync seams all deleted, exactly as colliders stopped
breaking the day they became child entities (§5).

**Corollary — Inspector-visible ⇒ Save-persisted ⇒ round-trip-owned.** If a
value shows up in the Inspector, Save must persist it; if Save persists it,
`load → save` must own it as a byte fixed point. A value that is editable but
not serialized (or serialized but not round-trip-stable) is a bug waiting to
surface as "my edit vanished on reload". The one data model is what makes this
hold for free: an authored value is a component, and components already
round-trip.

**The extension recipe (how to add a new authored thing).** Do NOT add a file
block or a bespoke editor subsystem. Instead:

1. **Define a component** with clearly named authored vs derived fields (author
   the source; recompute the derived — e.g. `CameraComponent.Zoom` is authored,
   the view matrix is derived; a collider's `Size` is authored, its world AABB
   derived).
2. **Register its serializer** (`ComponentSerializerRegistry` — engine types in
   `EngineComponentSerializers`, game types in the game's own registration),
   so it round-trips through the canonical serializer.
3. **Optionally add an Inspector default-initializer** so "Add ⟨component⟩"
   births a sane instance.

Those three steps buy the whole authoring stack — file authoring, Inspector
editing, undo, dirty-tracking, prefab overrides, byte-stable diffs, and
Game-mode sandbox protection — **by composition, not configuration**. There is
no fourth step and no special case. When a value seems to *need* a file block,
that is the signal it wants to be a component on an entity instead. (A legacy
block that predates this tenet is migrated forward by the CLI umbrella
`monodreams migrate` — the camera block's v2→v3 lift is the reference; see the
`level-editor` migrator premises.)

### Aspirational direction

The reserved `RunPartial` / `RuntimeEditable` policies are placeholders
for finer edit-time behavior (a system that does reduced work, or stays
interactive, while editing) — they run-as-`RunNormally` today and gain
distinct semantics when a later wave needs them. The interaction matrix
is enforced by review and by the editor screen's own tests until a
declarative system-dependency API (§2, §7) can validate it at
registration time.

3363	## Trigger zones are Passive colliders identified by an auto-numbered EntityInfo string
3364	
3365	A trigger zone (island-authoring §5.3 — evidence spot / talk radius / exit) is a **`Passive`
3366	box collider** whose identity rides **`EntityInfoComponent`** — `Type` = a game-defined category
3367	prefix (`"evidence"`, `"talkzone"`, `"exit"`, screen-supplied as `TriggerType`s) and `Name` = an
3368	auto-numbered scene-unique instance id (`"evidence_01"`, `TriggerFactory.NextName` = one past the
3369	highest existing suffix, so numbering survives deletes). **No new component**: the trigger IS a
3370	passive collider + a serialized identity string, exactly what a game reaction system pattern-matches
3371	on (the in-repo `ZoneDialogueTriggerSystem` precedent — a collision message + a zone identity → a
3372	game reaction). It round-trips through the existing `EntityInfo` + `BoxCollider` serializers
3373	unchanged (the `Passive` flag already serialises); rename is editing the saved JSON (banked decision
3374	3 — no free-text widget). Placement rides the palette's Place mode (a "Triggers section" of the
3375	strip); the placed zone is centred on the click, auto-selected, and one `CreateEntityCommand` undo
3376	step (auto-tagged `SceneObject`). Under colliders-as-entities the trigger IS a standalone collider
3377	ENTITY, so once placed it is re-selected by the ordinary collider **border-pick on its world shape** and
3378	moved/scaled by the ordinary gizmo (a `TransformEditCommand` on its own transform — Scale grows the box) —
3379	no proxy; like any box collider it refuses Rotate. A trigger is **Passive like all static geometry**, so the flag
3380	alone cannot tell a blocker from a sensor — the game's collision classifier decides that by identity
3381	(a known trigger prefix → a non-Physics collision type the physical resolver ignores → fires without
3382	blocking; everything else → Physics → blocks). Because a passive collider has no sprite and would be
3383	invisible in Edit, `TriggerOverlaySystem` draws an Edit-only tinted outline for every trigger (a
3384	Passive box `SceneObject` with no sprite) plus the armed-trigger placement ghost, on the
3385	native-resolution Editor target (the chrome rule: no `VisibleComponent`).
3386	
3387	**Why:** the plan's decision to reuse the engine's existing string identity + passive-collider
3388	mechanism instead of inventing a trigger component keeps the editor game-agnostic and matches the
3389	one working precedent; auto-numbering gives unique, stable ids without a text-input widget; the
3390	Edit-only outline is what makes an otherwise-invisible sensor visible and selectable.
3391	**Breaks:** a trigger that blocks the player (classified Physics, or the classifier keyed on the
3392	`Passive` flag — which every static blocker also sets); an invisible zone a designer can neither see
3393	nor select; a duplicate identity string two game systems can't disambiguate; a new component that
3394	the game's reaction system would have to learn instead of reading the string it already reads.

3397	round-trips through the serializers; a moving player entering the zone emits a `CollisionMessage`
3398	carrying the trigger's `EntityInfoComponent` identity) and the milestone test.

A trigger zone (island-authoring §5.3 — evidence spot / talk radius / exit) is a **`Passive`
box collider** whose identity rides **`EntityInfoComponent`** — `Type` = a game-defined category
prefix (`"evidence"`, `"talkzone"`, `"exit"`, screen-supplied as `TriggerType`s) and `Name` = an
auto-numbered scene-unique instance id (`"evidence_01"`, `TriggerFactory.NextName` = one past the
highest existing suffix, so numbering survives deletes). **No new component**: the trigger IS a
passive collider + a serialized identity string, exactly what a game reaction system pattern-matches
on (the in-repo `ZoneDialogueTriggerSystem` precedent — a collision message + a zone identity → a
game reaction). It round-trips through the existing `EntityInfo` + `BoxCollider` serializers
unchanged (the `Passive` flag already serialises); rename is editing the saved JSON (banked decision
3 — no free-text widget). Placement rides the palette's Place mode (a "Triggers section" of the
strip); the placed zone is centred on the click, auto-selected, and one `CreateEntityCommand` undo
step (auto-tagged `SceneObject`). Under colliders-as-entities the trigger IS a standalone collider
ENTITY, so once placed it is re-selected by the ordinary collider **border-pick on its world shape** and
moved/scaled by the ordinary gizmo (a `TransformEditCommand` on its own transform — Scale grows the box) —
no proxy; like any box collider it refuses Rotate. A trigger is **Passive like all static geometry**, so the flag
alone cannot tell a blocker from a sensor — the game's collision classifier decides that by identity
(a known trigger prefix → a non-Physics collision type the physical resolver ignores → fires without
blocking; everything else → Physics → blocks). Because a passive collider has no sprite and would be
invisible in Edit, `TriggerOverlaySystem` draws an Edit-only tinted outline for every trigger (a
Passive box `SceneObject` with no sprite) plus the armed-trigger placement ghost, on the
native-resolution Editor target (the chrome rule: no `VisibleComponent`).

**Why:** the plan's decision to reuse the engine's existing string identity + passive-collider
mechanism instead of inventing a trigger component keeps the editor game-agnostic and matches the
one working precedent; auto-numbering gives unique, stable ids without a text-input widget; the
Edit-only outline is what makes an otherwise-invisible sensor visible and selectable.
**Breaks:** a trigger that blocks the player (classified Physics, or the classifier keyed on the
`Passive` flag — which every static blocker also sets); an invisible zone a designer can neither see
nor select; a duplicate identity string two game systems can't disambiguate; a new component that
the game's reaction system would have to learn instead of reading the string it already reads.
**Tests:** `MonoDreams.Tests/LevelEditor/TriggerPlacementTests.cs` (`TriggerFactory` makes a passive
centred box with the prefix identity; `NextName` auto-numbers uniquely per prefix; the trigger
round-trips through the serializers; a moving player entering the zone emits a `CollisionMessage`
carrying the trigger's `EntityInfoComponent` identity) and the milestone test.

active body); foundation — `EntityInfoComponent` (string identity, serialized); this file — "The
component-serializer registry is opt-in per type" (the trigger uses only pre-registered serializers).

2420	## Viewport overlays are session settings; the grid IS the snap grid, bounded, and hidden while the Game tab is active
2421	
2422	The editor's viewport overlays — the world reference grid, the selection outline, and the camera-entity
2423	frustum glyph — are toggled by a per-session `ViewportOverlaySettingsComponent` on a standalone
2424	editor-state entity (`EditorInfrastructureComponent`-tagged, so it survives a transport Restart):
2425	`ShowGrid` (default **off** — preserves the current look), `OutlineSelected` (default **on**),
2426	`ShowCameraGlyph` (default **on**). It is deliberately **not** registered on the component-serializer
2427	registry — **session-scoped v1**; per-project persistence (writing these into the project manifest) is
2428	named terrain. The Scene-header **Overlays** dropdown (`EditorToolbarAction.Overlays`) and the ops
2429	`overlay:grid|outline|camera on|off` + `overlay:spacing <n>` drive the SAME settings through the pure
2430	`ViewportOverlayOps` (op channel + menu-path channel, one application each).
2431	
2432	**One grid quantum — spacing IS the snap step.** There is **no separate grid-spacing field**: the grid
2433	spacing is `GizmoStateComponent.GridStep` (the gizmo snap step). `EditorGrid` reads it, and BOTH the
2434	`overlay:spacing` op AND the menu's 8/16/32/64 presets WRITE it — so the displayed grid is always the
2435	grid things snap to, in both directions (change spacing via the menu → the gizmo snaps at the new step;
2436	change the snap step elsewhere → the grid follows). A second copy would let the overlay lie about where
2437	things snap.
2438	
2439	**The grid is bounded and gated.** `EditorGrid` bakes world-space lines at `GridStep` across the visible
2440	world AABB through the SAME overlay path as the gizmo/glyph (screen-baked on the native `Editor` target,
2441	viewport-clipped by `OverlayMeshClip`, identity `WorldMatrix`, **no** `VisibleComponent`), at the LOWEST
2442	overlay depth (`EditorTheme.Depths.Grid` = 0.01, beneath `ProxyOverlay`), every 5th line the stronger
2443	`GridMajor` role (else `GridMinor` — subtle warm darks, `Bg2..Border` on the ramp). The line count is
2444	**bounded** by the pure `GridGeometry` (pre-mortem #5): above ~200 minor lines/axis it degrades to
2445	major-only, above ~200 major lines/axis it draws nothing — a zoomed-out view over a small spacing can
2446	never allocate an unbounded mesh. The grid, the selection outline (`OutlineSelected` off → the outline
2447	emit is suppressed; the selection itself is unaffected), and the camera glyph (`ShowCameraGlyph` off →
2448	hidden; the view/camera divergence rule then applies only while on) are all **Edit-only**, and **all three
2449	are hidden while the Game tab is active (`ActiveContextKind == Game`)** — the sandbox looks like the game (Blender hides overlays in camera
2450	view). The gizmo/glyph gates are injected `Func<bool>` seams from the overlay (the systems stay
2451	game-agnostic); the grid emits from the draw-phase `EditorOverlayPrepSystem`, beneath the others.
2452	
2453	**Why:** the design §3 — Blender's per-viewport Overlays, adapted. The one-quantum rule is the load-bearing
2454	invariant: an overlay that draws a grid at a spacing DIFFERENT from the snap step misleads the designer
2455	about where a snapped drag lands. The bound keeps a pathological zoom from freezing the editor. The
2456	Game-mode hide keeps the sandbox faithful to the shipped view.
2457	**Breaks:** a second spacing value drifts from the snap step (the grid lies); an unbounded grid mesh at a
2458	zoomed-out view freezes/OOMs the editor; a `VisibleComponent` on the grid mesh pulls it into
2459	`MeshPrepSystem`, which overwrites the identity `WorldMatrix` its screen-baked vertices require; a grid
2460	(or outline, or glyph) left visible while the Game tab is active breaks "the sandbox looks like the game"; a raw
2461	`Color`/XNA token in `EditorGrid` trips the palette lint (it takes the `GridMinor`/`GridMajor` roles).
2462	**Tests:** `MonoDreams.Tests/LevelEditor/GridGeometryTests.cs` (`Plan_EmitsLinesAtSpacing_OverTheVisibleRange`,
2463	`Plan_MajorLines_AreEveryFifth_AnchoredToTheOrigin`, `Plan_DegradesToMajorOnly_ThenToNothing_AsTheRangeGrows`,
2464	`Plan_LineCount_IsAlwaysBounded_RegardlessOfZoom`); `MonoDreams.Tests/LevelEditor/ViewportOverlayTests.cs`
2465	(`Settings_Defaults_GridOff_OutlineOn_CameraOn`; the `overlay:*` + menu-path ops; `Op_Spacing_WritesTheSharedGridStep_NoSecondCopy`
2466	+ `Spacing_IsTheSnapStep_OneValue_BothDirections`; `REDACTED`,
2467	`Grid_FollowsTheSharedGridStep_ChangingItViaTheOpReSpacesTheGrid`, `Grid_ClipsToTheGameViewport_UnderAnInset_DevicePixelDestination`,
2468	`Grid_HiddenInPlay_AndWhenTheGateIsFalse`, `Grid_PathologicalZoomOut_DegradesToNothing_NoUnboundedMesh`,
2469	`Grid_ModerateZoomOut_StaysBounded_MajorOnly`; `OutlineSelectedOff_SuppressesOnlyTheOutline_HandleStays_SelectionUnaffected`,
2470	`GameMode_HidesAllGizmoOverlays_TheSandboxLooksLikeTheGame`, `CameraGlyphGate_Off_HidesTheFrustum_EvenWhenTheViewDiffersFromTheCamera`).
2471	**Depends on:** this file — "Editor context menus are a data-driven popup …" (the Toggle menu that drives
2472	these settings), "The gizmo applies a quantized (snap-on) or raw (snap-off) transform edit" (the
2473	`GridStep` this shares as the ONE grid quantum), "The editor visualizes + edits the scene camera ENTITY"
2474	(the frustum glyph this gates), "Selection picks MAX final `LayerDepth` …" (the gizmo whose outline this
2475	gates), "The editor shell insets the game viewport …" (the `OverlayProjection` + `OverlayMeshClip` +

2477	`GridMinor`/`GridMajor` roles + `Depths.Grid` + the lint), "The viewport context stack …"
2478	(the `ActiveContextKind == Game` hide); rendering — `LineMeshGenerator` + the mesh `DrawComponent` draw path.

2480	## The palette hold-drag multi-stamps at arc-length spacing, coalesced into one undo step
2481	
2482	While a palette sprite item is armed in `Place` mode, a **hold-drag** stamps the prop repeatedly:
2483	the press stamps one and opens a coalescing transaction (`EditorHistory.BeginTransaction`), holding
2484	+ dragging stamps more — one per `GizmoStateComponent.StampSpacing` of **arc-length** travelled,
2485	sampled by the pure `Brush/StrokeSampler` (which carries the leftover fractional distance between
2486	frames, so spacing is exact regardless of frame rate or cursor speed) — and the release commits the
2487	whole stroke as **exactly one** `CommitTransaction` history entry (one undo removes every stamp of
2488	the drag). A **single click** (press then release with no drag) is the degenerate case: one stamp,
2489	one undo step. This is the plain embryo of the future scatter brush — no jitter, no seed; each stamp
2490	is an ordinary `CreateEntityCommand` (auto-tagged `SceneObjectComponent`, sub-graph snapshot). A
2491	non-positive `StampSpacing` disables multi-stamp (a click still places one). Stamps that
2492	snap-collapse onto the previous position (snap on + spacing < grid) are skipped so identical props
2493	never stack in one cell; the last stamp is auto-selected on release. Any interruption of an open
2494	stroke (disarm, Escape/right-click, entering Play, dispose) **commits** it — the placed stamps are
2495	real edits, and an abandoned open transaction on the shared history would break the next
2496	`BeginTransaction`. Triggers (island §5.3) stay single-click, not multi-stamped.
2497	
2498	**Why:** dressing large areas (grass tufts, stones) one click at a time is the bottleneck the
2499	scatter brush will eventually solve; arc-length spacing is the minimal, jitter-free first step, and
2500	coalescing keeps one drag = one undo step (the gizmo's drag-coalescing contract, reused).
2501	**Breaks:** un-coalesced stamps make one drag N undo steps; frame-rate-dependent spacing clumps
2502	stamps where the cursor moved slowly; an abandoned open transaction throws on the next drag; stacking
2503	identical props in one grid cell when snap collapses the spacing.
2504	**Tests:** `MonoDreams.Tests/LevelEditor/StrokeSamplerTests.cs` (even spacing, diagonal, leftover
2505	carry-over, disable/short-segment no-op) and `MonoDreams.Tests/LevelEditor/PalettePlacementTests.cs`
2506	(`MultiStampTest_HoldDragStampsAtSpacingAndCoalescesToOneUndoStep` — a scripted hold-drag stamps at
2507	the expected spacing, nothing is committed mid-drag, the release is one undo step that one undo
2508	reverses whole; `PlacementTest_SingleClickIsOneUndoStepAutoSelectAndRepeat` — a single click still
2509	places one, one undo step, auto-selected).
2510	**Depends on:** this file — "Bounded undo with drag-coalescing" (the transaction pattern) and
2511	"Viewport presses belong to exactly one tool family" (multi-stamp acts only in `Place`).
2512	
2513	## `file:` AssetKeys load drop-folder art at runtime and graduate to content keys at ship
2514	
2515	A placed prop's `SpriteInfoComponent.AssetKey` may use the `file:` scheme
2516	(`"file:Island/props/tree01.png"`, optional `#region` suffix for a sliced-sheet entry): the
2517	texture is loaded at runtime — `Texture2D.FromStream` over `TitleContainer.OpenStream`, lazy and
2518	memoized per PNG (`FileAssetTextureLoader`) — from the gitignored asset drop folder
2519	(`Content/Island/`, copied raw to the output content dir; its committed `MANIFEST.md` names the
2520	packs). The catalog scan (`AssetCatalog.Scan`) reads **only** the directory listing + the
2521	`*.slices.json` sidecars, never a PNG (`TitleContainer` cannot enumerate, so the scan is
2522	host-filesystem — desktop-editor-first). A **missing file at load is a loud `Logger.Warning` plus
2523	the shared visible magenta placeholder texture, never an invisible entity**. The region suffix
2524	identifies the palette entry only — loading always opens the base PNG and the region's `Source`
2525	rect is serialized on the sprite itself, so scenes survive sidecar changes. When art finalizes,
2526	assets graduate into MGCB content and `file:` keys flip to content keys — a mechanical, greppable
2527	migration; `file:` is the fast-iteration authoring loop, content keys are the shipping (and
2528	web-ready) form.

named terrain. The Scene-header **Overlays** dropdown (`EditorToolbarAction.Overlays`) and the ops
`overlay:grid|outline|camera on|off` + `overlay:spacing <n>` drive the SAME settings through the pure
`ViewportOverlayOps` (op channel + menu-path channel, one application each).

**One grid quantum — spacing IS the snap step.** There is **no separate grid-spacing field**: the grid
spacing is `GizmoStateComponent.GridStep` (the gizmo snap step). `EditorGrid` reads it, and BOTH the
`overlay:spacing` op AND the menu's 8/16/32/64 presets WRITE it — so the displayed grid is always the
grid things snap to, in both directions (change spacing via the menu → the gizmo snaps at the new step;
change the snap step elsewhere → the grid follows). A second copy would let the overlay lie about where
things snap.

**The grid is bounded and gated.** `EditorGrid` bakes world-space lines at `GridStep` across the visible
world AABB through the SAME overlay path as the gizmo/glyph (screen-baked on the native `Editor` target,
viewport-clipped by `OverlayMeshClip`, identity `WorldMatrix`, **no** `VisibleComponent`), at the LOWEST
overlay depth (`EditorTheme.Depths.Grid` = 0.01, beneath `ProxyOverlay`), every 5th line the stronger
`GridMajor` role (else `GridMinor` — subtle warm darks, `Bg2..Border` on the ramp). The line count is
**bounded** by the pure `GridGeometry` (pre-mortem #5): above ~200 minor lines/axis it degrades to
major-only, above ~200 major lines/axis it draws nothing — a zoomed-out view over a small spacing can
never allocate an unbounded mesh. The grid, the selection outline (`OutlineSelected` off → the outline
emit is suppressed; the selection itself is unaffected), and the camera glyph (`ShowCameraGlyph` off →
hidden; the view/camera divergence rule then applies only while on) are all **Edit-only**, and **all three
are hidden while the Game tab is active (`ActiveContextKind == Game`)** — the sandbox looks like the game (Blender hides overlays in camera
view). The gizmo/glyph gates are injected `Func<bool>` seams from the overlay (the systems stay
game-agnostic); the grid emits from the draw-phase `EditorOverlayPrepSystem`, beneath the others.

**Why:** the design §3 — Blender's per-viewport Overlays, adapted. The one-quantum rule is the load-bearing
invariant: an overlay that draws a grid at a spacing DIFFERENT from the snap step misleads the designer
about where a snapped drag lands. The bound keeps a pathological zoom from freezing the editor. The
Game-mode hide keeps the sandbox faithful to the shipped view.
**Breaks:** a second spacing value drifts from the snap step (the grid lies); an unbounded grid mesh at a
zoomed-out view freezes/OOMs the editor; a `VisibleComponent` on the grid mesh pulls it into
`MeshPrepSystem`, which overwrites the identity `WorldMatrix` its screen-baked vertices require; a grid
(or outline, or glyph) left visible while the Game tab is active breaks "the sandbox looks like the game"; a raw
`Color`/XNA token in `EditorGrid` trips the palette lint (it takes the `GridMinor`/`GridMajor` roles).
**Tests:** `MonoDreams.Tests/LevelEditor/GridGeometryTests.cs` (`Plan_EmitsLinesAtSpacing_OverTheVisibleRange`,
`Plan_MajorLines_AreEveryFifth_AnchoredToTheOrigin`, `Plan_DegradesToMajorOnly_ThenToNothing_AsTheRangeGrows`,
`Plan_LineCount_IsAlwaysBounded_RegardlessOfZoom`); `MonoDreams.Tests/LevelEditor/ViewportOverlayTests.cs`
(`Settings_Defaults_GridOff_OutlineOn_CameraOn`; the `overlay:*` + menu-path ops; `Op_Spacing_WritesTheSharedGridStep_NoSecondCopy`
+ `Spacing_IsTheSnapStep_OneValue_BothDirections`; `REDACTED`,
`Grid_FollowsTheSharedGridStep_ChangingItViaTheOpReSpacesTheGrid`, `Grid_ClipsToTheGameViewport_UnderAnInset_DevicePixelDestination`,
`Grid_HiddenInPlay_AndWhenTheGateIsFalse`, `Grid_PathologicalZoomOut_DegradesToNothing_NoUnboundedMesh`,
`Grid_ModerateZoomOut_StaysBounded_MajorOnly`; `OutlineSelectedOff_SuppressesOnlyTheOutline_HandleStays_SelectionUnaffected`,
`GameMode_HidesAllGizmoOverlays_TheSandboxLooksLikeTheGame`, `CameraGlyphGate_Off_HidesTheFrustum_EvenWhenTheViewDiffersFromTheCamera`).
**Depends on:** this file — "Editor context menus are a data-driven popup …" (the Toggle menu that drives
these settings), "The gizmo applies a quantized (snap-on) or raw (snap-off) transform edit" (the
`GridStep` this shares as the ONE grid quantum), "The editor visualizes + edits the scene camera ENTITY"
(the frustum glyph this gates), "Selection picks MAX final `LayerDepth` …" (the gizmo whose outline this
gates), "The editor shell insets the game viewport …" (the `OverlayProjection` + `OverlayMeshClip` +
`Editor` target + the depth stack), "Every level-editor color and depth is an `EditorTheme` role" (the
`GridMinor`/`GridMajor` roles + `Depths.Grid` + the lint), "The viewport context stack …"
(the `ActiveContextKind == Game` hide); rendering — `LineMeshGenerator` + the mesh `DrawComponent` draw path.

## The palette hold-drag multi-stamps at arc-length spacing, coalesced into one undo step

While a palette sprite item is armed in `Place` mode, a **hold-drag** stamps the prop repeatedly:
the press stamps one and opens a coalescing transaction (`EditorHistory.BeginTransaction`), holding
+ dragging stamps more — one per `GizmoStateComponent.StampSpacing` of **arc-length** travelled,
sampled by the pure `Brush/StrokeSampler` (which carries the leftover fractional distance between
frames, so spacing is exact regardless of frame rate or cursor speed) — and the release commits the
whole stroke as **exactly one** `CommitTransaction` history entry (one undo removes every stamp of
the drag). A **single click** (press then release with no drag) is the degenerate case: one stamp,
one undo step. This is the plain embryo of the future scatter brush — no jitter, no seed; each stamp
is an ordinary `CreateEntityCommand` (auto-tagged `SceneObjectComponent`, sub-graph snapshot). A
non-positive `StampSpacing` disables multi-stamp (a click still places one). Stamps that
snap-collapse onto the previous position (snap on + spacing < grid) are skipped so identical props
never stack in one cell; the last stamp is auto-selected on release. Any interruption of an open
stroke (disarm, Escape/right-click, entering Play, dispose) **commits** it — the placed stamps are
real edits, and an abandoned open transaction on the shared history would break the next
`BeginTransaction`. Triggers (island §5.3) stay single-click, not multi-stamped.

**Why:** dressing large areas (grass tufts, stones) one click at a time is the bottleneck the
scatter brush will eventually solve; arc-length spacing is the minimal, jitter-free first step, and
coalescing keeps one drag = one undo step (the gizmo's drag-coalescing contract, reused).
**Breaks:** un-coalesced stamps make one drag N undo steps; frame-rate-dependent spacing clumps
stamps where the cursor moved slowly; an abandoned open transaction throws on the next drag; stacking
identical props in one grid cell when snap collapses the spacing.
**Tests:** `MonoDreams.Tests/LevelEditor/StrokeSamplerTests.cs` (even spacing, diagonal, leftover
carry-over, disable/short-segment no-op) and `MonoDreams.Tests/LevelEditor/PalettePlacementTests.cs`
(`MultiStampTest_HoldDragStampsAtSpacingAndCoalescesToOneUndoStep` — a scripted hold-drag stamps at
the expected spacing, nothing is committed mid-drag, the release is one undo step that one undo
reverses whole; `PlacementTest_SingleClickIsOneUndoStepAutoSelectAndRepeat` — a single click still
places one, one undo step, auto-selected).
**Depends on:** this file — "Bounded undo with drag-coalescing" (the transaction pattern) and
"Viewport presses belong to exactly one tool family" (multi-stamp acts only in `Place`).

## `file:` AssetKeys load drop-folder art at runtime and graduate to content keys at ship

A placed prop's `SpriteInfoComponent.AssetKey` may use the `file:` scheme
(`"file:Island/props/tree01.png"`, optional `#region` suffix for a sliced-sheet entry): the
texture is loaded at runtime — `Texture2D.FromStream` over `TitleContainer.OpenStream`, lazy and
memoized per PNG (`FileAssetTextureLoader`) — from the gitignored asset drop folder
(`Content/Island/`, copied raw to the output content dir; its committed `MANIFEST.md` names the
packs). The catalog scan (`AssetCatalog.Scan`) reads **only** the directory listing + the
`*.slices.json` sidecars, never a PNG (`TitleContainer` cannot enumerate, so the scan is
host-filesystem — desktop-editor-first). A **missing file at load is a loud `Logger.Warning` plus
the shared visible magenta placeholder texture, never an invisible entity**. The region suffix
identifies the palette entry only — loading always opens the base PNG and the region's `Source`
rect is serialized on the sprite itself, so scenes survive sidecar changes. When art finalizes,
assets graduate into MGCB content and `file:` keys flip to content keys — a mechanical, greppable
migration; `file:` is the fast-iteration authoring loop, content keys are the shipping (and
web-ready) form.

Wave 2 added the **native scene format** + the **component-serializer registry** (under `Serialization/`) and an additive `AssetKey` on `SpriteInfoComponent`. Wave 3 added the **scene round-trip** (`SceneObjectComponent`, `SceneWriter`, `LoadSceneRequest` + `SceneReaderSystem`, `IPlatformServices.ExportScene`). Wave 4a added the **interactive-editor substrate**: the reference editor composition (in `MonoDreams.Examples.Core`) of the gated game pipeline + editor systems in one world with an in-place `RunMode` flip; `SelectedComponent` + `EditorIdComponent` + `SelectionSystem` (click-to-pick the frontmost sprite); the `EditorHistory` bounded undo/redo with drag-coalescing + the `IEditorCommand` abstraction and the create/delete/transform commands; and `EditorCommandSystem`.
