The old HUD-virtual toolbar builder is retired. **Wave 8a** made the overlay **universal** (under the run flag every Examples screen composes it — the menu and the infinite runner included; the overlay can supply its own cursor pipeline to a cursor-less screen via `provideCursorPipeline`), made selection + the gizmo **target-aware** (UI/HUD-target sprites hit-test/drag in virtual space via `VirtualPosition`; across targets the composite order wins — UI/HUD above Main; the entity's own space selects the overlay projection), and shipped the **systems panel** (`System/SystemsPanelSystem` + the pure `UI/SystemsPanelLayout`) in the shell's right strip: every registrar entry of both pipelines, in order, as name + policy tag + live enabled checkbox, toggled through `EditorPipelineRegistrar.SetEnabled`. **Wave 8b** added the **collider gizmo proxies**: colliders are component-local spatial data (not entities), so `System/ProxySyncSystem` materializes standalone proxy entities (`GizmoProxyComponent` bindings under `Component/`, geometry under `Proxy/ProxyGeometry`) over the selected entity's collider shapes; they join the same selection pick (border-only hit-test) and the same gizmo drag (move tool), writing back into the bound component through `Undo/ColliderEditCommand` (one undo step per drag; convex writes refresh `WorldVertices`/`BroadPhaseAABB`). **Post-Wave-8b host wiring** extended the universal overlay **across hosts**: the Demos host (the launcher menu + all four module demo screens) composes it under the same run flag, pairing the overlay with the engine's new `DefaultEditorKeys` default keyboard surface (for hosts without their own action mapping) — the step-by-step recipe any new host/screen follows is [Adding the editor to a screen/host](#adding-the-editor-to-a-screenhost) below. The **transport model** (post-hands-on user directives) retired the F1 mode toggle and the menu's per-level "Edit" buttons / `LevelEditorScreen`: the run flag is the ONLY door, the shell is always visible under it, and `Composition/EditorTransport` owns `RunMode` through the toolbar's left-most **Play/Pause** (one label-swapping toggle button) + **Restart** buttons and the headless `Play`/`Pause`/`Restart` ops — Restart rebuilds the scene from the screen-recorded original load request (history cleared, world-level level components removed, scene entities disposed with `EditorInfrastructureComponent`-tagged/cursor/`KeepAlive` entities surviving; unsaved edits discarded; lands Paused). The **native-resolution overlays + HiDPI wave** (post-transport user directive: “the editor should be rendered at the native screen resolution … like Flutter … gizmos and entity boundaries too”) moved every editor overlay VISUAL (gizmo handles, selection outline, proxy outlines) off the virtual-resolution Main target onto the Editor layer — screen-baked each frame by the draw-side `editor.overlayPrep` pass (`System/EditorOverlayPrepSystem` → `GizmoSystem.EmitOverlays`/`ProxySyncSystem.EmitOverlays`) through the pure `Transform/OverlayProjection` + `Transform/OverlayMeshClip` — and made the whole editor device-pixel aware: on macOS Retina `Composition/EditorHiDpi` re-backs the window at device resolution under the run flag (stock DesktopGL is logical-size + OS-upscaled), `ViewportManager.DevicePixelRatio` carries the ratio, `CursorInputSystem` scales `ScreenPosition` into backbuffer pixels, and the chrome layouts/fonts multiply their point metrics by it. **Island-authoring Slice 1** (the game-anchored phase — see `docs/level-editor/island-authoring-plan.md`) added the **asset palette + placement loop**: an `Assets/` catalog of a gitignored drop folder (`AssetCatalog.Scan` — one entry per PNG plus `*.slices.json` sidecar regions; scan never opens a PNG), runtime `file:` AssetKeys loaded lazily through `Assets/FileAssetTextureLoader` (missing file = loud warning + a visible magenta placeholder, never invisible; `SceneReaderSystem` rehydrates `file:` keys through it), the generic `Assets/SpritePropFactory` (standard prop stack from a catalog entry + a screen-supplied `Assets/PaletteBand`; feet-origin on Y-sorted bands), the coarse **tool modality** `EditorToolMode` on the shared `GizmoStateComponent` (`SelectTransform`/`Place`; selection + gizmo early-out outside `SelectTransform`), the bottom-strip **palette chrome + ghost + click-place** (`System/PalettePlacementSystem` + the pure `UI/PaletteLayout`; placement = one `CreateEntityCommand` undo step, auto-selected; Escape/right-click disarm; headless `palette:<id>` / `band:<name>` ops via the overlay's named dispatch), and the **save guard** (Save is blocked, loudly, while the transport is Playing). **Island-authoring Slice 2** added **order and shape**: within-band ordering (toolbar Bring forward / Send back, headless `order:forward`/`order:back`, PageUp/PageDown on `DefaultEditorKeys` — `EditorCommandSystem` nudges the SOURCE sort fields by `OrderStep`, clamped inside the band via the new `DrawLayerMap.TryGetBandRange`; a Y-sorted band nudges `YSortDepthBias`, never `LayerDepth`, through one `Undo/SpriteSortEditCommand` per click), the **proxy `(kind, index)` generalization** (`ProxySyncSystem` keys its family by kind + element index; per-vertex `ProxyBindingKind.ConvexVertex` handles materialize while the convex family's proxy is selected, and a vertex drag writes back exactly one model vertex — non-convex results rejected loudly, see the premise), **box collider resize handles** (eight edge/corner handles on the box proxy, pure `Proxy/BoxResize` math, one-drag-one-undo through `ColliderEditCommand`), and the **collider authoring actions** (toolbar +Box/+Poly/-Col/+Vtx, headless `collider:*` — footprint default = full sprite width x bottom quarter, feet-anchored, pure `Proxy/ColliderDefaults`; add/remove through the snapshotting `Undo/ColliderComponentCommand`; Delete retargets on proxies: a vertex proxy deletes its vertex with the >= 3 guard, a shape proxy removes its bound collider). **Island-authoring Slice 3** added **walk the island**: the freeform **boundary tool** (`EditorToolMode.Boundary` + `System/BoundaryToolSystem` — click-lay a polyline with a live preview, Enter/double-click commits as one undo step into a `Component/BoundaryComponent{Points,Thickness}` authoring entity, Escape/right-click cancels; per-vertex editing via the reused `(kind,index)` proxy family, `ProxyBindingKind.BoundaryVertex`, on plain selection), the message-driven **`System/BoundaryBakeSystem`** (reacts to the boundary component added/changed → one thin **passive** convex quad segment collider per polyline edge as `ChildOf` `Component/BakedProductComponent` children — static world geometry that blocks; the pure math is `Boundary/BoundaryGeometry`; **bake products are never serialized** — `SceneWriter` excludes them even inside the tagged root's `ChildOf` closure — and re-bake on load/edit, in both run modes), the **trigger palette** (screen-supplied `Assets/TriggerType`s in a palette "Triggers section"; placing one drops a `Passive` box + an auto-numbered `EntityInfoComponent` identity via `Assets/TriggerFactory`; `System/TriggerOverlaySystem` draws the Edit-only tinted outlines + placement ghost; headless `boundary:begin|commit|cancel` and `trigger:<prefix>` ops), and the **walkable-island milestone** verified end-to-end (`IslandMilestoneTests`: build → save → reload → Play walk blocked by coast + footprint, triggers fire with the right identity → Restart rebuilds). The **colliders-as-entities phase (CE-A–CE-D)** then turned a collider into a first-class ENTITY (a shape + its own `TransformComponent`, `ChildOf` a body; box = centered `Size`, no offset) and retired the Wave-8b whole-shape proxy layer: a collider is border-picked and moved/scaled by the ordinary gizmo, **Add Collider ▸ Box/Polygon** creates a child collider entity, `−Col` deletes it, and only convex vertex grips remain proxies — see [`docs/level-editor/colliders-as-entities.md`](../../../docs/level-editor/colliders-as-entities.md). Anything not yet built is marked **(planned, Wave N)**.
53:- `CameraNavSystem` (post-Wave-A, live, under `System/`) — Edit-guarded camera navigation: middle-mouse **pan** (the camera moves opposite the cursor's virtual-pixel delta, scaled by `1/Zoom`, so the grabbed world point stays put), scroll-wheel **zoom** (a geometric step on `Camera.Zoom`, clamped 0.25–4.0), and the public **`FrameScene()`** method that centres + zoom-fits the camera on the AABB of all `SpriteInfoComponent` content (no content = no-op) — triggered by the `EditorShortcuts` **Home** binding or the headless `view:frame` op (UX3-E), NOT a keyboard predicate on this system. Drives `Camera.Position`/`Zoom` directly (the editor owns the camera in Edit; `CameraFollowSystem` is `Freeze`-gated). Registered **before `CursorPositionSystem`** so the camera mutation is the camera the cursor's world-pos derives from that same frame. Inert in Play.
102:- `LoadSceneRequest` (Wave 3, live, under `Message/`) — loads a native MonoDreams scene file; distinct from `LoadLevelRequest` so it never triggers the LDtk `Content.Load` / `Remove<CurrentLevelComponent>` path. Carries the scene `Path` and a `FromContent` flag (content asset vs. host-filesystem user data).

## The palette lists assets as cards (icon on top, label on the bottom) in a scrollable grid

The palette's bottom strip renders each catalog entry as a fixed-size **card** — a lazily-loaded art
**thumbnail** filling the top icon box, the **text label** on the bottom row (truncated with an
ellipsis to the card width so it never bleeds into the neighbour; the label-only fallback when the
texture is missing/magenta), and a small **band-chip badge** in the icon's top-right corner showing
the per-asset band mark (a band initial when marked, `-` when unmarked; click cycles it — see the
resolution premise above). Cards flow left-to-right into a fixed-width grid inside
`EditorChromeLayout.BottomBar` and scroll by **whole card rows** on the mouse wheel (scrolled-out rows
are parked off-screen — no clipping). The band-selector header row stays at the top of the strip. The
pure grid math (card rects, icon/label/chip sub-rects, column wrap, whole-row scroll, DPR scaling)
lives in `PaletteLayout` so it is unit-testable without a GraphicsDevice. `EditorChromeLayout.BottomBarHeight`
was raised (104 → 168 logical points) to give the cards real screen real estate — the game viewport
inset shrinks by the same amount, automatically, because the shell + mouse mapping both derive from
`ViewportInset`. Hit-testing is card-body-then-chip: a click on the chip cycles the band (never
arms), a click anywhere else on the card arms placement. **UX-B:** the shelf height is now the
runtime `EditorShellStateComponent.BottomHeightPt` (the bottom splitter resizes it) and the palette
renders in the shelf **body below its "Assets" tab strip** (`EditorChromeLayout.RegionBody`); when
the cards overflow, the palette draws the same slim `Border`/`BorderStrong` scrollbar as the right
strip (draggable, sharing the shell drag token — the shell-state premise), and it stands down while
any foreign splitter/scrollbar drag owns the pointer. **PF-D:** the shelf's tab strip is now
interactive (`Assets | Prefabs`, OWNED by this system — the retired static tab left
`EditorChromeBuilder`); the **Prefabs** tab lists `.mdprefab` cards (a prefab glyph + id) and reuses the
SAME `Place`-mode arm/ghost/click machinery (mutually exclusive with an armed asset/trigger; the prefab
ghost v1 is none — click-on-viewport). Each tab's chrome parks when the other is active. See "The prefab
UX … (PF-D)". **PF-F — the palette is now UNIVERSAL:** when a screen supplies NO catalog/bands of its own
but the project context is resolved, the OVERLAY builds them itself — a default catalog scanned from the
`Content/Island` drop-folder convention (`EditorOverlay.DefaultAssetDropFolder`) + one band per layer of
the SCREEN's own `DrawLayerMap` (`EditorOverlay.DefaultBandsFromLayers`) — so a menu / demo gets the
Assets + Prefabs tabs too, not just the game screen (the user's "the editor should be oblivious to what
kind of scene is loaded"). An unresolved project keeps the no-palette behavior; a screen that supplies
its own catalog/bands overrides it; the screen still weaves `overlay.Palette` into its pipeline.

**Why:** the user's report that the palette assets "should be bigger, take a little more height … and
be actual cards with the icon/preview on top and text on the bottom" — flat text rows are hard to
scan and give the art no room. Keeping the layout math pure keeps it testable and keeps chrome
hit-tests aligned at any DPR.
**Breaks:** an inset that grows only compositing (not mouse mapping) desyncs every world pick by the
extra bottom margin; a card grid computed in the system (not `PaletteLayout`) can't be unit-tested;
an un-truncated label bleeds across cards; a chip hit-test after the card body would arm instead of
marking.

## Save is blocked while Playing, while the Game tab is active, or when no project root is resolved

`EditorOverlay.DispatchToolbarAction`'s Save case no-ops with a loud `Logger.Warning` in THREE
distinguishable cases (`EditorOverlay.SaveBlock(state, projectContext, activeKind)` →
`SaveBlockReason.Playing` / `SaveBlockReason.GameMode` / `SaveBlockReason.NoProjectRoot`, checked in
that precedence): (1) while `RunMode == Play` — saving
is an authoring act over the **paused** scene, and a mid-Play save would bake transient run state (a
mid-air player, in-flight velocities, half-resolved collisions) into the scene file as if it were
authored truth; (2) while the **Game tab is active** (PF-B, `ActiveContextKind == Game`) — sandbox edits
are expressly not-to-be-saved (they discard on leave), so Save reflects the real Scene tab, not the
sandbox (see "The viewport context stack …"); (3) while the editor's `EditorProjectContext` is unresolved
(no `game.mdproj` found — a shipped/relocated build, a console, or an unset `MONODREAMS_PROJECT_ROOT`
with nothing to walk up to) — there is nowhere versioned to write. The toolbar renders the Save button
dimmed for ANY cause (the transport rule dims all editing buttons while Playing; a small per-button
gate additionally dims Save while Paused-but-blocked — `NoProjectRoot` OR `GameMode`), and this guard
closes the remaining dispatch paths (the
headless `ToolbarAction` op, any programmatic dispatch). The two reasons are reported separately so

## Conventions

- **Commit/PR language:** en
- **Conventional commits:** yes (`type(scope): description` — e.g. `feat(web):`, `fix(level-ldtk):`, `refactor(web):`)
- **Branch naming:** `type/kebab-slug` or `ro/kebab-slug` (e.g. `feat/kni`, `ro/convex-collider-sat`)
- **PR body:** keep PRs focused — one module or one premise per PR is ideal. Update tests,
  premises, and `postInstallNotes` in the same PR that changes behavior. See `CONTRIBUTING.md`
  › "Filing issues and PRs".
- **Test conventions:** `dotnet test MonoDreams.Tests/`; integration tests use headless replay +
  log assertions via `GameTestRunner` (`AssertLogContains`, `AssertLogContainsInOrder`); headless
  demo self-verification via `GameTestRunner.RunDemosAsync` + `AssertScreenshotNonBlank` /
  `AssertHeapFlat`. See `CONTRIBUTING.md` › "Tests" and `.claude/CLAUDE.md` › "Testing".
- **Commit trailer:** `Co-Authored-By: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>`

git add -A && git commit -m "$(cat <<'EOF'
feat(level-editor): fit-and-finish — TriggerType.Configure seam, undoable Restart, placement fixes, grid fade

Port of the reference implementation (roo-oliv/gmtk-2026gj), scoped to
issue #50's four items:

1. TriggerType.Configure + ActiveLayers — the seam that keeps the engine
   clean: a game supplies an optional Action<Entity> hook (and collision
   layers) on its trigger types, so one palette click authors a fully
   functional game object while the module stays ignorant of what it
   built. Empty ActiveLayers = a pure marker (selectable, collides with
   nothing).

2. Undoable Restart — EditorTransport captures the world as SceneData
   before the teardown and pushes ONE RestartUndoCommand onto the
   just-cleared history via the new EditorHistory.PushApplied (record
   without re-applying; refused inside a transaction). Ctrl+Z restores
   the pre-restart world through the reader's sweep/rebuild/restore
   delegates; redo re-runs the reload-from-disk. Exactly one level deep;
   graceful no-push when the snapshot seams aren't wired.

3. Two placement fixes — the active bottom tab joins the palette's
   layout cache key (a programmatic panel:tab switch re-lays the shelf
   instead of leaving Assets chrome painted over the Prefabs tab), and
   drag-stamping gains a per-stroke visited set plus a cross-stroke
   duplicate-cell guard (a wobbling drag never doubles a cell;
   re-clicking a filled cell is a loud-logged no-op).

4. Grid density fade — minors step toward invisible as their on-screen
   spacing shrinks (majors carry the packed grid), with the fade applied
   PREMULTIPLIED via the lint-blessed Color.Lerp(Transparent, role, a)
   (a raw new Color(...) would trip EditorThemeLintTests; straight alpha
   would read brighter, not fainter, on the mesh path).

Premises updated in the same PR (the seam note, restart-undo, the
dedupe guards, the density fade, the layout-cache-key invariant) with
the nine new tests wired into their Tests: fields.

Closes #50

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.REDACTED
EOF
)" && git push -u origin issue-50

## 1. `TriggerType.Configure` + `ActiveLayers` — the seam

`TriggerType` gains two additive init-properties: `Action<Entity>? Configure` (a game hook invoked on the freshly-built trigger entity, after the standard `EntityInfo` + `Transform` + `BoxCollider` stack) and `int[]? ActiveLayers` (scopes the placed box's collision layers; empty = a pure marker that collides with nothing; null = the collider default). `TriggerFactory.Create` applies both. One palette click now authors a fully functional game object while the module stays ignorant of what it built. All existing call sites construct positionally, so behavior is unchanged for them.

**Doc note (premises):** `Configure` is documented as THE sanctioned way a game teaches the palette to build its objects.

## 2. Undoable Restart

- New `Undo/RestartUndoCommand.cs` — holds the pre-restart `SceneData` snapshot; `Revert` restores it through the reader (the same sweep → `RebuildCodeContent` → `RestoreSnapshot` delegates a tab switch uses), `Apply` re-runs the teardown + reload-from-disk (redo).
- `EditorHistory.PushApplied` — records a command WITHOUT invoking `Apply` (the restart already ran); refused inside a coalescing transaction.
- `EditorTransport.Restart` captures the snapshot via the stack's existing `CaptureSnapshot` seam BEFORE `_history.Clear()`, and pushes the one surviving undo entry after the reload. Exactly one level deep; screens without the snapshot seams wired restart exactly as before (nothing pushed).

**Noted behavior (inherited from the reference, kept as-is):** with the seams wired, the dirty indicator lights immediately after a Restart — the pushed entry bumps the edit version past the save point. Zoomed out, the grid congealed into a solid wall of lines. Minors now fade in steps as their on-screen spacing shrinks (≥48px full → ≥24px 0.55× → ≥12px 0.3× → gone; majors carry the packed grid), from a quieter 0.55 base alpha. **What shipped** (all four items ported from `gmtk-2026gj`, coded by three parallel Opus agents, verified centrally):

If you'd rather have "restart lands clean, undo reads dirty", it's a one-line `MarkSavePoint()` after the push — say the word and I'll add it.

Docs rode in the same PR: five premise updates in `level-editor/docs/premises.md`, including the issue's mandated note that `Configure` is *the* sanctioned way a game teaches the palette to build its objects, plus a new layout-cache-key invariant the placement work surfaced. **Rebase done, conflicts resolved, and PR #70 is MERGEABLE again** (head `2b99572` on top of current main).

What the rebase involved:

- **One file had textual conflicts** — `PalettePlacementTests.cs` (a usings line and the class doc comment, where main's layers wave and my new test bullets met). Resolved by keeping both sides.
- **The engine files auto-merged, and I verified the hot spot semantically**: `StampAt` is where my duplicate-stamp guards met main's new layers-wave parenting (`EnsureActiveSpritesLayer`). The merged result came out byte-identical to the reference implementation — which carries both features — so the convergence is provably right, not just compiling. I also confirmed my new tests' assumptions against main's updated helpers (the layer bootstrap adds no undo entry; `PlacedProps` already excludes layer entities; the constructor signature is unchanged).

**One thing you should know: main's test gate is currently red, independent of this PR.** The full Release run on the rebased branch came back 1222/1223, and the single failure is `EditorThemeLintTests.EveryModuleColorIsAThemeRole_NoRawColorsOutsideEditorTheme` — it flags five raw `Color.White` tokens in `TileGridBakeSystem.cs`, which the tile-grid merge (`75c2a0f`, PR #71) placed inside `level-editor` where the theme lint scans. That file is byte-identical between main and this branch; all 70 tests in the five classes this PR touches pass. So merging #70 neither fixes nor worsens it.

If you want, I can open a small separate PR replacing those `Color.White` tints with a theme role (or a lint-blessed token) to get main green again — say the word.

name: publish
on:
  workflow_dispatch: # Allow running the workflow manually from the GitHub UI
  push:
    branches:
      - 'main'       # Run the workflow when pushing to the main branch
  pull_request:
    branches:
      - '*'          # Run the workflow for all pull requests

      - published    # Run the workflow when a new GitHub release is published

env:
  DOTNET_SKIP_FIRST_TIME_EXPERIENCE: 1
  DOTNET_NOLOGO: true
  NuGetDirectory: ${{ github.workspace }}/nuget

defaults:
  run:
    shell: pwsh

jobs:
  create_nuget:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v3
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0 # Get all history to allow automatic versioning using MinVer
      
      # Install the .NET SDK indicated in the global.json file
      - name: Setup .NET
        uses: actions/setup-dotnet@v4
      
      # Create the NuGet package in the folder from the environment variable NuGetDirectory
      - run: dotnet pack --configuration Release --output ${{ env.NuGetDirectory }}
      
      # Publish the NuGet package as an artifact, so they can be used in the following jobs
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v3
        with:
          name: nuget
          if-no-files-found: error
          retention-days: 7
          path: ${{ env.NuGetDirectory }}/*.nupkg

  validate_nuget:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: [ create_nuget ]
    steps:
      # Install the .NET SDK indicated in the global.json file
      - name: Setup .NET
        uses: actions/setup-dotnet@v4

      # Download the NuGet package created in the previous job
      - uses: actions/download-artifact@v3
        with:
          name: nuget
          path: ${{ env.NuGetDirectory }}

      - name: Install nuget validator
        run: dotnet tool update Meziantou.Framework.NuGetPackageValidation.Tool --global

      # Validate metadata and content of the NuGet package
      # https://www.nuget.org/packages/Meziantou.Framework.NuGetPackageValidation.Tool#readme-body-tab
      # If some rules are not applicable, you can disable them
      # using the --excluded-rules or --excluded-rule-ids option
      - name: Validate package
        run: meziantou.validate-nuget-package (Get-ChildItem "${{ env.NuGetDirectory }}/*.nupkg")

  run_test:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v3
      - name: Setup .NET
        uses: actions/setup-dotnet@v4
      - name: Run tests
        run: dotnet test --configuration Release

  deploy:
    # Publish only when creating a GitHub Release
    # https://docs.github.com/en/repositories/releasing-projects-on-github/managing-releases-in-a-repository
    # You can update this logic if you want to manage releases differently
    if: github.event_name == 'release'

    needs: [ validate_nuget, run_test ]
    steps:
      # Download the NuGet package created in the previous job
      - uses: actions/download-artifact@v3
        with:
          name: nuget
          path: ${{ env.NuGetDirectory }}

      # Install the .NET SDK indicated in the global.json file
      - name: Setup .NET Core
        uses: actions/setup-dotnet@v4

      # Publish all NuGet packages to NuGet.org
      # Use --skip-duplicate to prevent errors if a package with the same version already exists.
      # If you retry a failed workflow, already published packages will be skipped without error.
      - name: Publish NuGet package
        run: |
          foreach($file in (Get-ChildItem "${{ env.NuGetDirectory }}" -Recurse -Include *.nupkg)) {
              dotnet nuget push $file --api-key "${{ secrets.NUGET_APIKEY }}" --source https://api.nuget.org/v3/index.json --skip-duplicate
          }#nullable enable

**Done — PR [#72](https://github.com/roo-oliv/monodreams/pull/72) is open**, with the full suite green (1223/1223 — the run that's red on main today). Two focused commits:

1. **`fix(level-editor)`** — the five bare `Color.White` tokens in `TileGridBakeSystem.cs` (the streamed-tile sprite tint + the four merged-quad vertex colors) now take `EditorTheme.NeutralTint`, the role the theme already ships for untinted-texture draws. Zero visual change (`NeutralTint == Color.White`); the module keeps one color source and the lint is green.

2. **`ci`** — `publish.yml` is gone; `ci.yml` replaces it with only the `run_test` job (tests on pushes to main, PRs, and manual dispatch). The `create_nuget`/`validate_nuget`/`deploy` jobs, the `release` trigger, and the `NuGetDirectory` plumbing are all removed. I kept the job name `run_test` identical so any branch-protection required-check config keeps matching without edits.

One sequencing note: PR #70 (issue #50) was rebased before this fix existed, so its CI run will still show the pre-existing lint failure until #72 merges. Merging **#72 first**, then re-running #70's checks (or letting a merge-queue rebase handle it), gets both green with no extra work. The worktree is back on `issue-50`.

content.text:
**TL;DR: PR #72 didn't break anything — `run_test` has been failing on every run of this repo's CI, including all of main's recent merges. The old workflow's red was attributed to the broken `create_nuget` job, but `run_test` was failing underneath it all along. Your PR just made it visible by leaving `run_test` as the only job.**

Evidence:

- I checked the per-job conclusions of an older main run (the merge of #68, before any of today's work): `run_test` = **failure**, `create_nuget` = failure, rest skipped. Every listed run of `publish.yml` — main merges and PR branches alike — is red.
- On PR #72's run, the failures are exclusively the ~13 **integration tests that spawn a real game process**: `NativeSceneBootTests`, `HeadlessDemoTests`, `ContentTreeIsolationTests`, `DemosEditorOverlayTests`. Everything in-process passes (the CLI suite is 47/47, and the theme-lint fix itself is green — the lint test isn't among the failures).

Why those tests fail on the runner: the exit codes tell the story. The spawned games die with **exit 134 (SIGABRT)** or exit 1, and one demo never exits and hits the 120-second timeout. GitHub's `ubuntu-latest` runner has **no display server**, and MonoGame DesktopGL initializes SDL video even in this repo's headless modes — the headless contract is a real 1×1 off-screen window plus a `GraphicsDevice`, which needs a video driver and GL context. No display → SDL init throws → the runtime aborts. On your Mac these same tests pass (we just ran 1223/1223 locally) because there's a real windowing system.

The standard fix is to give the runner a virtual display — Mesa's software GL is already on GitHub runners, so it's a one-line change in `ci.yml`:

```yaml
- name: Run tests
  run: xvfb-run -a dotnet test --configuration Release
```

(plus dropping `shell: pwsh` if kept, since `xvfb-run` wants bash). If some game-spawning test still misbehaves under software GL, the fallback is to exclude `IntegrationTests` from the Linux CI run and treat the local macOS full gate as the authority for those.

Want me to add the `xvfb-run` change to PR #72 and see if it turns the run green?

content.content:
## Headless Demos renders every frame; capture reads the backbuffer

The Demos host's `Draw` must **not** early-return in headless mode
(unlike the Examples host, whose headless `Draw` is a no-op). Headless
Demos keeps a real `GraphicsDevice` backed by a full-virtual-resolution
backbuffer (the window is hidden off-screen at `(-2000, -2000)`, never
relied on for presentation), and runs the full prep→`MasterRenderSystem`
→`FinalDrawSystem` pipeline every frame. `ScreenshotCaptureSystem` then
reads that composited backbuffer. The backbuffer must stay at the virtual
resolution (not 1×1) or the read-back is meaningless.

**Why:** the entire point of the headless observe path (issue #28) is to
let an agent verify visual/runtime claims without a human. A no-op `Draw`
or a 1×1 backbuffer renders nothing to read back — exactly the gap in the
Examples headless mode. MonoGame DesktopGL 3.8.4 has no null graphics
device, so a hidden full-res window is the achievable form of "headless
render".
**Breaks:** early-returning `Draw`, or shrinking the headless backbuffer
to 1×1, makes every captured PNG blank and hides render-path memory
behaviour — the leak class #27 documents becomes unobservable again.
**Tests:** `MonoDreams.Tests/IntegrationTests/HeadlessDemoTests.cs`.
**Depends on:** rendering — "`MasterRenderSystem` is the sole renderer";
"Rendering systems run last in the pipeline".

## Headless heap samples measure the live set, not transient churn

Demos keeps a real `GraphicsDevice` backed by a full-virtual-resolution
backbuffer, and runs the full prep→`MasterRenderSystem`
→`FinalDrawSystem` pipeline every frame. `ScreenshotCaptureSystem` then
reads that composited backbuffer. The backbuffer must stay at the virtual
resolution (not 1×1) or the read-back is meaningless. The window is never
relied on for presentation and is **hidden via `HeadlessWindow.Hide`**
(`SDL_HideWindow` on the live SDL window — the GL context and backbuffer
stay renderable): the old `(-2000, -2000)` position move alone is kept
only as the fallback, because macOS clamps off-screen positions back onto
the display, leaving visible windows a user could accidentally click
during a local test run. On a display-less CI runner the tests run under
`xvfb-run` (SDL still needs a video device to create the window at all).

The full suite + CLI tests are green too. From now on, local test runs shouldn't flash any game windows on your Mac.

`EditorThemeLintTests` was red on main since the tile-grid merge (#48 / PR #71): `TileGridBakeSystem.cs` carries five bare `Color.White` tokens inside `level-editor`, where the palette lint forbids raw color tokens. ## 2. `ci`: retire NuGet packaging/publishing — the engine ships shadcn-style

`create_nuget` / `validate_nuget` / `deploy` (and the `release` trigger) date from the NuGet-package era and were broken; since the engine moved to shadcn-style source distribution via the `monodreams` CLI there is no package to publish. `publish.yml` → `ci.yml`, only `run_test` survives (same job name, so required-check config keeps matching).

## 3. `fix(debug)`: headless runs hide the OS window — SDL_HideWindow locally, xvfb on CI

`run_test` failed on every CI run ever: the integration tests spawn real games, and MonoGame DesktopGL initializes SDL video even in headless mode — display-less runners abort (SIGABRT). CI now runs under `xvfb-run -a`. The same contract was broken the other way locally: the `(-2000,-2000)` off-screen position trick doesn't survive macOS (Cocoa clamps positions back on-screen), so spawned test games flashed focusable windows the user could accidentally click. **CI is green on PR #72 — [run 31030282446](https://github.com/roo-oliv/monodreams/actions/runs/31030282446), the first passing `run_test` in this workflow's history.** The PR description is updated to cover the full story, and I've recorded the new verify knowledge in memory.

Heads are now Release-pre-built once per test process (core first, per the repo rule) and spawned with `--no-build` — which also made the local integration suite ~25% faster.

And from your earlier ask: local test runs now hide spawned game windows via `SDL_HideWindow` (`HeadlessWindow.Hide`), so nothing pops up to click by accident on your Mac — verified by the non-blank screenshot assertions still passing with hidden windows.

content.text:
Yes, there's a proper fix, and it's pushed (`ce1f3ea` on PR #72). The subtlety: hiding the window can't stop the focus steal, because on macOS the focus grab happens at **app activation during SDL video init** — before any window exists to hide. SDL has a dedicated switch for exactly this: the `SDL_MAC_BACKGROUND_APP` hint, which launches the game as an *accessory app* — no Dock icon, no menu bar, and crucially **no activation**, so your typing in the browser is never interrupted.

What went in:

- **`HeadlessWindow.PreventFocusSteal()`** — sets the hint via its environment variable. It must run before the `Game` object is constructed (SDL initializes inside the `Game` base constructor), so both heads' `Program.cs` call it first thing under `--headless`, and `GameTestRunner` also sets the env var on every spawn as belt-and-braces. It never overrides an explicitly set value and is a no-op off macOS.
- **`InactiveSleepTime = TimeSpan.Zero`** in both heads' headless branches — a corollary bug this surfaced: a hidden, never-activated window makes `Game.IsActive` false, and MonoGame throttles inactive games to ~50fps (20ms/frame), which had been quietly violating the documented headless max-speed contract ever since the windows went hidden. Headless now never sleeps on inactivity.
- The debug-module premise documents both mechanisms.

Verified locally: build clean, all 27 integration tests pass (1m23s). You can confirm the feel by running `dotnet test MonoDreams.Tests/ --configuration Release --filter "FullyQualifiedName~IntegrationTests"` while typing somewhere — nothing should take your focus now. CI is running on the commit; I'll report when it concludes.
